---
title: "Download the data"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, comment = "#>")
library(jnanalytics)
repo <- "najkoja/jn_analytics"
hf <- paste0("https://huggingface.co/datasets/", repo)

# File list of the current release on Hugging Face, read when the site is
# built; the release table is read only once the first release is uploaded
api <- paste0("https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/", repo)
tree <- jsonlite::fromJSON(paste0(api, "/tree/main?recursive=true"))
available <- "release.parquet" %in% tree$path
if (available) {
  file <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
  utils::download.file(paste0(hf, "/resolve/main/release.parquet"), file, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  release <- as.data.frame(arrow::read_parquet(file))
}
```

All tables of jnanalytics are published as [Parquet](https://parquet.apache.org/)
files in the Hugging Face dataset
[`najkoja/jn_analytics`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics):
the reference tables, the journal-level aggregates and the article tables
(`articles`, `article_first_authors`, `article_agreements`). They can be read
without an account or API key, in R, Python, DuckDB or any other tool that
reads Parquet. The same tables are in BigQuery,
`subugoe-collaborative.jn_analytics`.

Data and code are released under CC0.

## Current release

```{r, results = "asis"}
if (!available) {
  cat("The first release on Hugging Face is in preparation.\n")
}
```

```{r, eval = available}
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Item = c(
      "Version", "Built", "Crossref snapshot", "OpenAlex snapshot",
      "JCT snapshot", "Publication years"
    ),
    Value = c(
      release$version, format(release$snapshot_date), release$crossref_snapshot,
      release$openalex_snapshot, release$jct_snapshot,
      paste(release$pub_year_min, release$pub_year_max, sep = "–")
    )
  )
)
```

The links below point to the latest release. Every release is a tagged
commit named after its build date. Read an earlier release with
`.../resolve/<date>/<file>` instead of `.../resolve/main/<file>`, or with
`--revision <date>` in `hf download`.

```{r, results = "asis"}
tags <- jsonlite::fromJSON(paste0(api, "/refs"))$tags$name
if (length(tags) > 0) {
  cat("Releases:", paste0("`", sort(tags, decreasing = TRUE), "`", collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

## Files

```{r, eval = available}
files <- tree[tree$type == "file" & grepl("\\.parquet$", tree$path), ]
files$table <- ifelse(dirname(files$path) == ".", sub("\\.parquet$", "", files$path), dirname(files$path))
tables <- intersect(c(jn_publish_tables(), "release"), files$table)
size_mb <- vapply(tables, function(t) sum(files$size[files$table == t]) / 1e6, numeric(1))
n_files <- vapply(tables, function(t) sum(files$table == t), numeric(1))
download <- ifelse(
  n_files == 1,
  paste0("[", tables, ".parquet](", hf, "/resolve/main/", tables, ".parquet)"),
  paste0("[", tables, "/](", hf, "/tree/main/", tables, ") (", n_files, " files, one per year)")
)
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Table = paste0("[`", tables, "`](data-model.html#", gsub("_", "-", tables), ")"),
    Size = ifelse(size_mb < 0.1, "< 0.1 MB", sprintf("%.1f MB", size_mb)),
    Download = download
  ),
  align = c("l", "r", "l")
)
```

The article tables are split into one file per publication year
(`pub_year`), for example `articles/articles_2025.parquet`. Read a single
year, or the whole folder at once. For questions about one agreement or
institution, start with `agreement_institution_year` (counts per
participating institution) and `agreement_articles` (the eligible works
themselves, with journal, type and OA status, sorted by agreement); both
need no joins.

Every table and column is described in the [data model](data-model.html),
including the counting rules. Two matter most when working with the files:

- Counts can be summed over journals, years and work types; compute shares
  from the sums. Filter `work_type` to `article` and `review` for research
  articles.
- The country tables count a work once per first-author country (full
  counting). Take totals from `journal_year`, never by summing over countries.

## Usage

### DuckDB

DuckDB reads the files directly from Hugging Face, including all years of an
article table at once:

```sql
SELECT pub_year, oa_model,
       sum(articles) AS articles,
       sum(articles_oa) / sum(articles) AS share_oa
FROM 'hf://datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/journal_year.parquet'
WHERE work_type IN ('article', 'review')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL;

SELECT oa_status, count(*) AS n
FROM 'hf://datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/articles/*.parquet'
WHERE pub_year = 2025 AND issn_l = '0360-0300'
GROUP BY ALL;
```

### R, with jnanalytics

Download the dataset with the [Hugging Face
CLI](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/guides/cli) (`brew install
hf` or `pipx install huggingface_hub`), all of it or only some tables:

```sh
hf download najkoja/jn_analytics --repo-type dataset --local-dir jn_data
hf download najkoja/jn_analytics --repo-type dataset --local-dir jn_data \
  --include "journal*.parquet" "agreement*.parquet" "portfolios.parquet" "release.parquet"
```

Then use the analysis functions; the article tables work too:

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(jnanalytics)
src <- jn_source("jn_data")
jn_oa(src, by = c("pub_year", "oa_model"))

jn_tbl(src, "articles") |>
  dplyr::filter(issn_l == "0360-0300", pub_year == 2025) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

### R, with arrow

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
url <- "https://huggingface.co/datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/resolve/main/journal_year.parquet"
download.file(url, "journal_year.parquet", mode = "wb")
journal_year <- arrow::read_parquet("journal_year.parquet")
```

### Python

With pandas and huggingface_hub installed:

```python
import pandas as pd

journal_year = pd.read_parquet("hf://datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/journal_year.parquet")
articles_2025 = pd.read_parquet("hf://datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/articles/articles_2025.parquet")
```

Or with the datasets library, one configuration per table:

```python
from datasets import load_dataset

journal_year = load_dataset("najkoja/jn_analytics", "journal_year")
```

## Column descriptions in the files

Each file carries its column descriptions as JSON in the Parquet metadata
(`jn_columns`), together with the table name (`jn_table`) and the package
version (`jn_version`):

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
meta <- arrow::open_dataset("journal_year.parquet")$schema$metadata
jsonlite::fromJSON(meta$jn_columns)
```
